title: Multi-Team Agentic Coding / Lead Agents

extraction.policy: Full native 4K (3840x2160) for every frame, no upscaling. PNG (lossless) used for the 5 UI-heavy / small-text IDE frames; JPEG q2 for the 6 chat-UI frames with larger text.

frames.label: ping-orchestrator-leads-cost
frames.transcript_anchor: 1:46-2:20 — 'ping' -> Orchestrator pong; 'ping each team lead' -> two-layer fan-out; footer sums orchestrator/leads/contacts/total cost.
frames.why_for_weak_student: The hook: you type `ping` and only the Orchestrator answers ('Pong. Teams are online — Planning, Engineering, Validation standing by'), then `ping each team lead` fans out. Footer shows Orch cost/context. The single-interface chat room before any complexity.

frames.label: lead-domain-block-delegate
frames.transcript_anchor: 2:36-3:37 — Engineering Lead steps out of its domain, is blocked, delegates to Backend/Frontend Dev; 'three tiers of agents'.
frames.why_for_weak_student: The three-tier money shot: the Engineering Lead's file tool calls show red X's (domain-blocked), it says 'I have restricted tool access as a lead — let me delegate this to my team members who have the right tools,' then @Backend Dev takes over. Proves leads delegate, never execute.

frames.label: toggle-workers-team-tree
frames.transcript_anchor: 3:45-4:20 — '/toggle workers' reveals the full team breakdown; agents load memory/expertise on boot.
frames.why_for_weak_student: `/toggle-workers` reveals all 10 agents with per-agent cost AND model: Orch/leads on claude-opus-4-6, workers on claude-sonnet-4-6. One image proves the roster, the model tiering, and per-agent cost tracking. Above the tree, the orchestrator's synthesis summarizes the classifier codebase (325 examples, ~85% accuracy, no HIGH->LOW inversions).

frames.label: classifier-predict-route
frames.transcript_anchor: 4:23-5:47 — the prompt-routing classifier; `just predict summarize this codebase` -> label medium with confidences.
frames.why_for_weak_student: The demo PROBLEM made concrete: `just predict "summarize this codebase"` -> Label: MID (circled), confidences {high 0.35, low 0.19, mid 0.45}, Routes to: claude-sonnet-4-6. Shows why the target codebase exists ('don't pay for intelligence you don't need') before the teams work on it. README pane shows 'The Problem'. PNG for the small terminal text.

frames.label: ask-all-teams-fanout
frames.transcript_anchor: 6:17-7:15 — 'ask all teams: two additional scikit-learn classifiers'; 'it wrote the exact same prompt to every single team'.
frames.why_for_weak_student: Multi-perspective in one frame: the Orchestrator writes the SAME question to @Planning, @Engineering, @Validation, each domain-tailored (product goals/latency; training/inference speed; testability/regressions). Shows consistent fan-out and why three teams beat one answer.

frames.label: orchestrator-agent-config
frames.transcript_anchor: 12:42-13:14 — open orchestrator.md: name, model, expertise, max-lines, skills, tools.
frames.why_for_weak_student: How an agent expert is DEFINED, in one screen: orchestrator.md frontmatter — model (anthropic/claude-opus-4-6), expertise (updatable, max-lines 10000), the 5 skills with use-when, tools, and domain (read/upsert/delete). The best 'anatomy of an agent' frame. PNG for legibility. NOTE: this on-screen version predates the tilldone integration (tools show read/grep/find/ls/delegate; no tilldone/write/edit) — the shipped file adds them.

frames.label: validation-security-review
frames.transcript_anchor: 15:41-16:31 — QA Engineer + Security Reviewer weigh in independently; security 'ship it, no issues'; different agents find different things.
frames.why_for_weak_student: The validation team working autonomously: Validation Lead delegates to Security Reviewer, who returns a structured review table and 'Ship it. No blocking issues.' Footer shows the whole team's costs mid-run. Different specialists, different context windows, different findings — and trust in autonomous review.

frames.label: active-listener-10-files
frames.transcript_anchor: 19:21-19:40 — 'I have this inside of every team member... all active listeners. Read the conversation log before every response.'
frames.why_for_weak_student: Skills composition made visible: a search for active-listener.md returns '10 results in 10 files' — every one of the 10 agents shares that one skill. Proves 'change one line, change many agents.' PNG for the search-panel text.

frames.label: frontend-domain-lock
frames.transcript_anchor: 21:14-22:01 — front-end/back-end domain shown side by side; 'read the back-end, but never touch it'; front-end can only write to the front-end directory.
frames.why_for_weak_student: Domain locking made concrete: frontend-dev.md with tools (incl. bash) and a domain scoped so it can write to apps/frontend/ but only READ the rest of apps — the exact 'read the back-end, never touch it' rule Dan types live. PNG for the small YAML. NOTE: this live edit differs from the shipped frontend-dev.md (which has plain apps/ r+u+delete, same as backend).

frames.label: conversation-jsonl-log
frames.transcript_anchor: 23:30-24:37 — open the session's conversation.jsonl + per-agent session files + templated system prompt; the session directory as shared space.
frames.why_for_weak_student: Conversation awareness made real: the actual conversation.jsonl with from/message/to/type/timestamp rows for user, orchestrator, and every lead/member — plus the session dir tree (per-team folders + complementnb-benchmark-plan.md + head-to-head-results.md the team wrote). Shows the shared log + session workspace. PNG for the dense JSON.

frames.label: head-to-head-cost-tiering
frames.transcript_anchor: 24:12-26:20 — head-to-head results (LR vs ComplementNB) written to sessions/.../head-to-head-results.md; 'leads as Opus, workers as Sonnet'; the ~$8 total cost.
frames.why_for_weak_student: The payoff + the cost: real ML eval results delivered by the team ('LR owns LOW, ComplementNB owns MID... LR stays as default, CNB a credible challenger'), and the footer showing Orch $8.280 total with Opus leads / Sonnet workers. This is the '$8 agent team' Dan defends — value delivered vs tokens spent.
